stories.research_notes:
Here are verified facts for the candidate story: “Iowa Stops Hunger recap: Table to Table rescues 2.7 million pounds of food”  

---

### What happened  

- According to Table to Table’s *FY 24 Annual Report* (July 2023–June 2024), the organization delivered (rescued and redistributed) **2.7 million pounds of food** in that fiscal year. ([table2table.org](https://table2table.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/FY24-FINAL-Annual-Report-Online.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- Table to Table is a food-rescue nonprofit in Iowa City whose mission is to reduce environmental harm and increase food equity by collecting surplus edible food and distributing it through partners who serve people facing food insecurity. ([table2table.org](https://table2table.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/FY24-FINAL-Annual-Report-Online.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

---

### Supporting evidence & context  

- The *Food Waste Prevention & Management Study* by the Iowa Department of Natural Resources reports that — for the “most recent year (typically 2023 at time of interviews)” — Table to Table accepted and distributed **2,700,000 pounds of food**. ([iowadnr.gov](https://www.iowadnr.gov/media/8921/download?inline=&utm_source=openai))  
- From their FY 24 report:  
  • They increased the quantity of food rescued and delivered to 2.7 million pounds. ([table2table.org](https://table2table.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/FY24-FINAL-Annual-Report-Online.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
  • About 60% of that food was classified as “highly-sought after” items — produce, protein, and dairy. ([table2table.org](https://table2table.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/FY24-FINAL-Annual-Report-Online.pdf?utm_source=openai))  

---

### What this *is not*  

- This is **not** a pledge, plan, or estimate — it is a completed outcome: 2.7 million pounds were actually rescued and delivered during fiscal year 2023-2024. ([table2table.org](https://table2table.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/FY24-FINAL-Annual-Report-Online.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- It is not limited to a single donor, or a forthcoming event; it is the summary of past performance.  

---

If you want, I can also pull up related data like meal equivalents, cost-savings, or comparisons from prior years.
stories.verified_headline: Table to Table rescues 2.7 million pounds of food in Iowa
stories.verified_summary: Table to Table rescued and redistributed 2.7 million pounds of food in the fiscal year 2023-2024, significantly impacting food insecurity in Iowa.
stories.verification_note: The claim is supported by multiple independent sources confirming the food rescue figures and the organization's mission.

stories.research_notes:
Here is a research note summarizing what actually has been established so far regarding “abundant saline infusion after thrombolysis” in acute ischemic stroke.

---

## What has been completed (measured outcomes)

1. **Preliminary (“pilot”) study from Taiwan**  
   - Published in *Emergency Medicine International* in April 2025. This single-arm interventional study involved 20 acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients treated with rt-PA who showed evidence of hypovolemia (measured by elevated blood urea nitrogen–creatinine ratio, BCR>15) compared to a historical control group of 170 similar patients. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12041639/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Intervention: after rt-PA, the treatment arm got enhanced hydration with 0.9% NaCl at 20 mL/kg body weight (one-third as bolus, rest over 8 hours), then maintenance at 40-80 mL/h over the next 16 hours. Control patients received standard hydration (40-60 mL/h over the first 24 h). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12041639/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Outcome at 3 months: 45.0% of the enhanced hydration group achieved favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] ≤2), compared to 21.2% in the control group. This difference was statistically significant (p = 0.018). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12041639/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Early neurological deterioration (END) (worsening NIHSS ≥4 within 72 hours): no significant difference between groups (10.0% vs. 10.6%, p=0.661) in the full AIS population; subgroup analysis showed benefits in the lower-severity group (NIHSS 4-10) but not in higher severity (NIHSS 11-24). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12041639/?utm_source=openai))  
   - Safety: No patient in the enhanced hydration group had major adverse events such as heart failure, pulmonary edema etc., and complication rates were not significantly different between groups. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12041639/?utm_source=openai))  

2. **NS-STAR / NS-STROKE (China)**  
   - This is a *completed* Phase II randomized controlled trial conducted by Tianjin Medical University General Hospital (3 sites in China), registered as NCT05993078 (“NS-STAR”) targeting **acute ischemic stroke** treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) with a large saline infusion (2,000 mL normal saline at 200 mL/h) vs control (200–400 mL NS) immediately after IVT. ([syfrah.com](https://www.syfrah.com/trial/NCT05993078?utm_source=openai))  
   - Results: According to a dataset published Aug 7, 2025, the NS-STROKE trial found that "early administration of abundant intravenous normal saline" after thrombolysis *improved 90-day outcomes* without increasing risk of death or cardiac dysfunction. ([data.mendeley.com](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/mkf7ffnb2z/1?utm_source=openai))  
   - Data details: primary outcome was favorable functional independence at 90 days (mRS 0-2 vs 3-6). Secondary outcomes included NIHSS changes, early neurological deterioration, imaging/lab metrics, mortality etc. Safety endpoints included intracranial hemorrhage, blood pressure fluctuations, etc. ([syfrah.com](https://www.syfrah.com/trial/NCT05993078?utm_source=openai))  

---

## What remains a launch/planned / not yet fully established

- **Phase III trial** (“NS-STROKE-2”, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07497542) is planned (or recently initiated) to test “immediate abundant intravenous normal saline infusion” (2,000-2,500 mL) vs small volume (≤600 mL) after thrombolysis. Enrollment and completion dates are in the future (2026-2029). No results yet. ([clinicaltrials.gov](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07497542?lastUpdPost=2020-01-10_&utm_source=openai))  
- Previous hydration trials (e.g. “REVIVE”) had tested enhanced vs standard hydration based on BUN/Cr criteria, but not specifically *immediately after* thrombolysis, or with such large bolus saline volumes; those did **not** show improved outcomes at 72 hours for early neurological deterioration. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11528967/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Conclusion

- There **is evidence** from both pilot/interventional and randomized trials that abundant (large-volume) normal saline infusion *after thrombolysis* may improve functional recovery (e.g. mRS 0-2 at 90 days) in acute ischemic stroke, **without major safety signals**—particularly in patients with mild to moderate stroke severity and evidence of hypovolemia.  
- However, the strongest evidence so far remains preliminary (small sample in Taiwan) and phase II RCTs (NS-STAR). A large multicenter randomized phase III is planned; its completion (expected ~2029) is needed for definitive confirmation.  

---

If you want, I can retrieve more details (e.g. numbers needed to treat, confidence intervals) or assess the trial designs and limitations.
